plan.thesis: A rotating machine has no operating point until it is connected to something, and every number that follows from it, the power, the suction margin, the stage count, the discharge temperature, is a consequence of where that point landed and of which limit was allowed to put it there. The discipline is knowing which limit set your answer, and whether the machine will still be there in a year.

tiers.beginner: Associate. THE PUMP AND THE SYSTEM IT WORKS INTO. Why: this is the only place in the Facilities module where a whole answer is assembled from two objects that are each incomplete on their own. A pump curve says what the machine makes and a system curve says what the piping demands, and neither has an operating point; the duty is SOLVED as their intersection, and the power, the conversion to pressure and the judgement of where the duty landed all hang off that one solved number. It is also the tier where the two field packagings, 2.31 and 3960, turn out to be one constant. The tier ends before the suction side, which is where selections actually fail.
tiers.intermediate: Professional. THE SUCTION SIDE, THE CHANGES, AND THE SECOND MACHINE. Why: a duty point that works on paper fails in three ways, and this tier is all three. It fails on suction, where NPSH available is built from the real suction side and the margin over required is not the same thing as adequacy. It fails on change, where a speed change follows the affinity laws exactly and a trim does not, and where applying either law to a duty point does not give you a new duty point because the system curve did not move. And it fails on the fluid, because a catalogue curve is a water curve. The tier ends with two pumps in parallel delivering far less than twice one pump, which is the result the engine exists to make visible.
tiers.advanced: Expert. THE COMPRESSOR, AND WHERE BOTH ENGINES STOP. Why: compression is the same discipline with the fluid no longer incompressible and the machine no longer describable by a curve the user can type in, so every answer comes out of a thermodynamic path instead of an intersection. The polytropic exponent is not the isentropic one; the stage count is the larger of two limits and the engine names which; the train can break the very temperature limit it was staged against. Then the audit: eighteen returns that come back non-finite with no error key, two refusals that name the wrong cause, a validity window one module in this package enforces and this one does not, two values of one gas constant, and a gate that compares a value with itself.

beginner: m01 What these engines size, and what they refuse (4 lessons). Two machines and two modules, and the scope seam said out loud: there is no surge line, no recycle, no seal or bearing calculation, no machine curve and no wheel selection anywhere in this package, and the Compressor studio's own help guide says so. Every refusal message in both modules, verbatim.

m02 Two curves, and why neither has an operating point (5). The system curve stated through a friction head at a flow rather than an abstract coefficient; the least-squares quadratic through catalogue points, what its R squared means and when it is null; the conditioning of the solve behind it, which is a different question from the fit; the shutoff head; and the droop flag the duty point reads.

m03 The duty point, solved (5). The intersection and the report the solve leaves behind (bracket, residual, halvings, converged); why that flag is made of the residual as well as the bracket, with the case that makes it false; the three refusals that are real answers, a pump that cannot start its system, a pair of curves that do not cross below the search limit, and a curve that does not droop; and what moves the point.

m04 Power, head and pressure (4). Hydraulic, brake and motor input power; the two field packagings measured out of the engine; and the single water density they both imply, printed with the difference between them.

m05 Where the duty landed (5). The four regions either side of best efficiency flow, what each costs in the engine's own words, the boundaries, and why the region is judged per machine and not on the combined flow.
m06 The Associate reading (3). One pump end to end, the capstone worked, and what the suction side changes.
intermediate: m01 NPSH available, from the real suction side (5). The pressure head over the vapour pressure, the static height and the suction friction; the flashing warning; and why an available figure on its own decides nothing.

m02 The margin, and what a check does not check (4). The customary rule, the three severities, why NPSHr is itself measured at a three percent head drop so bare equality is already cavitation, and what the check returns when it is handed an available head it cannot read.

m03 A speed change and a trim are not the same thing (5). The exact cube law against the trim shortfall, with the exactness printed as a subtraction; ideal and real side by side; the efficiency the trim's return implies, computed and returned rather than left to division; the vendor limit the warning names; and the two decimal boundaries and the slack that makes them land where the rule says.

m04 An affinity law applied to a duty point is not a new duty point (4). The system curve does not move when the machine changes, so the answer is a new intersection and not a scaled old one, and the scaled old one is a real point on the new curve that the machine will not run at. Both, labelled, and how far apart they get.

m05 Two pumps, and a catalogue curve that is a water curve (5). Parallel adds flow at equal head and series adds head at equal flow, and on a friction-dominated system the second machine buys far less than double; then the Hydraulic Institute correction, its correlating parameter, its three factors and its two warnings.
advanced: m01 A stage is not a pump (5). The polytropic exponent against the isentropic one and what using the wrong one costs; the discharge temperature that follows; compressibility evaluated at both ends and averaged; both heads reported so neither is quoted as the other; and why the two power routes agreeing is an algebraic identity rather than a check.

m02 The stage count, and the limit that governs (5). The equal-ratio rule, the discharge-temperature limit, the engine naming which one bound, the twelve-stage cap, and the closed form the search is converging on.

m03 The train, its cooling, and the limit that buys the stages (5). Equal ratios chained, interstage cooling as a real exchanger duty, and the comparison the whole of staging turns on: the stage count is tested at the inlet the stages will really have, so a hotter approach buys a machine rather than a hotter discharge. Then the trade that reverses: colder suction means less work and more heat to take out at a FIXED stage count, and the opposite across a stage-count change.

m04 The machine, the driver and the fuel (4). Actual inlet volume and why it falls with pressure; the four screening branches including the honest 'either', each reached by a duty that fails the three tests above it; the driver's fuel taken out of the stream being compressed; and the thermal efficiency the first law bounds, with the refusal boundary that IS the Btu in a horsepower-hour.

m05 What a refusal is, and where each guard turns over (4). Every refusal is a returned object naming the input that is wrong; the three bare-number functions that have nowhere to put one and hold a documented NaN contract instead; four faults that used to share one sentence and now have four; the compressibility window one module in this package declares and this one imports; and a gate that could not fail beside one that can.

capstones.beginner: A crude transfer pump against a stated station. The catalogue points, the static head, the friction head at its stated flow, the specific gravity and the pump efficiency are all given. Graded: the duty flow, the duty head, the hydraulic power, the brake power, the motor input in kilowatts, and the duty head expressed as a discharge pressure.
capstones.intermediate: The same station's suction side and a proposed speed change. The suction pressure, the vapour pressure, the static suction height, the suction friction and the speed ratio are all stated. Graded: the pressure-head component of NPSH available, NPSH available, NPSH available again at a stated raised suction pressure, the flow after the speed change, the head after the speed change, and the duty flow of two identical machines in parallel solved as a fresh intersection.
capstones.advanced: A gas compression train. The rate, suction pressure and temperature, discharge pressure, gas gravity, k, the polytropic and mechanical efficiencies, the maximum ratio per stage, the maximum discharge temperature, the intercooling approach and the driver heat rate and fuel heating value are all stated. Graded: the polytropic exponent ratio, the ratio per stage, the first stage's discharge temperature, the first stage's polytropic head, the first stage's gas horsepower, and the driver fuel in MMscfd.
capstones.heldItemCheck: NONE of the eighteen reads a held item, and each held item is neutralised by construction rather than by hope. (1) The HYDRAULIC INSTITUTE viscosity correction is an unsourced empirical form, so no capstone runs it and no graded field is a corrected flow, head or efficiency. (2) The TRIM SHORTFALL model has no publication behind it, so the Professional capstone grades a SPEED change, where the affinity laws are exact, and never a trim. (3) The OPERATING REGION bands at 50, 70, 120 and 140 percent are customary and unsourced, so no graded field is a region, a percentage of best efficiency flow or a verdict. (4) The NPSH MARGIN RULE, the larger of 3 ft and 35 percent, is customary and unsourced, so the Professional capstone grades NPSH AVAILABLE and never the required margin, the pass flag or the severity. (5) The comparison of the engine's implied water density to a published water density is held, but the packagings themselves are the engine's own definitions, so a power and a pressure conversion are gradeable. (6) The MACHINE SCREENING thresholds (500 and 20000 acfm, ratios of 4 and 6, 200 and 10000 bhp) are unsourced, so no graded field is a recommendation. (7) The compressor capstone's suction and discharge states are chosen INSIDE the DAK validity window, Tpr between 1.0 and 3.0 and Ppr at or below 30, and the capstone generator must assert that rather than assume it, because this module does not check it. (8) The three discriminating conditions, the maximum ratio per stage, the maximum discharge temperature and the intercooling approach, are STATED in the prompt, so no graded value depends on a default. (7) IS NOW ALSO ENFORCED BY THE ENGINE at 4fa37e6, which refuses outside the DAK window by name; the capstone's own assertion is kept as a second opinion on the CASE rather than on the engine, because a case edited later must still land inside the window. (9) NEW: the capstone also asserts that every curve it fits droops, that every duty solve reports converged, that the fit's R squared is finite, and that the graded speed change carries no extrapolation warning, so no graded answer can come off an unresolved solve or a curve the engine has disowned.

ids: fc-pump-explorer (Associate): the two curves on one axis with the crossing marked, the duty solved as that crossing, the power chain, and the four regions

fc-suction-explorer (Professional): NPSH available assembled from its three parts, the margin and its severities, a trim against a speed change with the ideal beside the real, parallel and series re-solved, and the Hydraulic Institute factors

fc-compressor-explorer (Expert, with the inlet-volume view open to Professional): the two staging limits and which governed, the train stage by stage with its cooling duty, the machine screen, the driver fuel, and the domain limits

plan.reCut: 2026-09-16, onto engines 4fa37e6. THREE MODULES CHANGE SUBJECT because the defects they were built on were repaired, and one gains a subject the repair created. Expert m05 was 'What these engines accept and should not', five lessons on unguarded inputs; thirty-one of those inputs now return a named error, so it is re-cut onto digest Section 15: what a refusal IS, the contract, the messages, the boundary either side of every guard, and the three bare-number functions that hold a documented NaN contract instead. Expert m03 was 'the limit it can break'; the train no longer breaks the limit it was staged against, and the better lesson is the one the repair exposed: a warmer intercooler approach is paid for in STAGES, and the cooling-against-power trade reverses across a stage-count change. Professional m04 was written when the Pump studio showed two answers for one change; Suite PR #491 labelled them as two questions, so the module teaches the distinction rather than the disagreement. Associate m03 gains the solve's own report: bracket, residual, iterations, converged, and a negative control showing a flag made only of the bracket could never be false.
